To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a multinomial hidden Markover model (MHMM), used with several yeast gene expression datasets, identifies statistically significant temporal dynamics and is more robust to missing data than linear decomposition methods.

we have developed a novel method, called the multinomial HMM, that can be used to deconvolve microarray gene expression data into contributions of pure cell populations, and that the deconvolution method identified statistically significant temporal gene expression dynamics.

a novel hidden-state Markov model for cell population deconvolution is able to extract temporal dynamics of gene expression in pure populations, and that this method can be used to identify novel genes involved in cell cycle regulation.

developing methods for deconvoluting gene expression data from complex biological processes and provides a novel approach for analyzing time series microarray data.
the development of a new method for cell population deconvolution and its application to the identification of temporal patterns of gene expression.

the development of novel statistical methods for analyzing gene expression data, particularly time series data, with the goal of improving our ability to extract biological knowledge from microarray experiments.
